answer: Treat each verified unit of computation as a ticket, rather than paying each account. Epoch randomness seeds memory-hard puzzles; each solution is bound to that epoch and can be redeemed once. Whether workers call themselves zenith, orchard, or haven, rewards and voting weight depend only on valid tickets. Splitting one machine among a thousand identities adds no tickets. More influence requires more RAM time and electricity, so an attacker must buy scarce computation instead of free names.
